Paragraph:
Translation: Therefore, O mighty-armed, one whose senses are restrained from their objects is certainly of steady intelligence.

Purport (Excerpt): As enemies are curbed by superior force, similarly, the senses can be curbed not by any human endeavor, but only by keeping them engaged in the service of the Lord...
Situation/Problem_Faced: Concluding the analysis on sensory turbulence and solidifying what establishes a person in steady intelligence.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna directly addresses Arjuna as 'mighty-armed,' challenging him to use that strength to completely restrain the senses from harmful objects. True intelligence is confirmed when sensory boundary enforcement becomes absolute.
Outcome/Resolution: A clear diagnostic standard is established for identifying a candidate fit for liberation (sadhaka).

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Boundary Enforcement: Restraining senses completely from detrimental objects
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Mastery Over Triggers: Neutralizing sensory threats through superior focus
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Psychological Readiness: Becoming a fit candidate for higher states of freedom

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Sadhaka (A practitioner prepared for spiritual realization)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: The ultimate sign of a steady mind is the complete, effortless restraint of the senses from their objects. This is achieved not through dry human ego, but by subduing the senses with the superior power of devotional service.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Concluding the section on mental stability, this verse defines true strength. Real power is not physical conquest; it is the capacity to erect firm boundaries between your internal peace and external temptations. When you can restrict your senses at will, your intelligence reaches a stable, resilient state.
